reason: S1 introduces a public error_code-returning get(T &) protocol and removes the prior get(T &, error_code &) form, but H0 never invokes the new overloads. Its typed extraction uses get<T>().first only after type() selects a matching type, so fuzz bytes cannot exercise the new output-assignment protocol or its type-error states. This is a commit-induced API-protocol gap; the unrelated historical lack of parse_many/load_many coverage is not attributed to this commit.
evidence: In include/simdjson/error.h, S1 adds simdjson_result_base<T>::get(T &) and simdjson_result<T>::get(T &), both returning error_code.
In include/simdjson/dom/element.h, S1 replaces element::get(T &, error_code &) with element::get(T &) returning error_code and makes the analogous change to simdjson_result<dom::element>.
In include/simdjson/inline/error.h, the new get(T &) calls tie and returns its error, while tie now assigns value only when !error.
fuzz_dump.cpp calls element.get<T>().first for a type already selected by element.type(); none of H0 calls element.get(value) or simdjson_result.get(value).

H0 does call parser.parse(...).tie(elem, error), so the changed tie implementation is reached, but that does not cover the newly introduced get(T &) entry points or mismatched-type output/error behavior.
recommended_action: Extend a DOM harness to call element::get(T &) and simdjson_result<dom::element>::get(T &) across both matching and deliberately mismatched JSON types, checking returned error codes while allowing fuzz input to control the element type and value.
